description: Harden the webhook delivery against SSRF via DNS rebinding by pinning the outbound connection to a pre-validated public IP. Independent of FEAT-001 but touches the same file (apps/api/src/services/webhookDelivery.ts) and its test, so runs after FEAT-001. Chosen approach: built-in node:https with a custom lookup that returns only validated public IP(s) — undici is NOT a dependency and NOT importable here, so true pinning via node:https avoids adding a dependency while keeping TLS certificate validation against the original hostname (SNI/servername default to the hostname; rejectUnauthorized stays true). https.request does not auto-follow redirects, preserving the existing redirect:"manual" guarantee. Keep the 10s timeout, https-only, hostname blocklist, and create-time validation.
steps: In apps/api/src/services/webhookDelivery.ts add pure `selectPinnedAddresses(resolved: Array<{ address: string; family: number }>): { ok: true; addresses: Array<{address:string;family:number}> } | { ok: false }` returning ok:false if resolved is empty or ANY address classifies as "blocked" (via existing classifyAddress), else ok:true with all addresses. Add async `resolveAndPinHost(host: string): Promise<Array<{address:string;family:number}>>`: if host is a literal IP (isIP), classify it and return [{address:host,family}] or throw WEBHOOK_URL_INVALID if blocked; else lookup(host,{all:true}), run selectPinnedAddresses, throw WEBHOOK_URL_INVALID (same message style) when not ok, else return the addresses.

Refactor assertSafeWebhookUrl to delegate its per-address loop to selectPinnedAddresses so create-time and send-time use one source of truth; preserve its existing throws, messages, https-only check, and isBlockedHostname check exactly.

In apps/api/src/services/webhookDelivery.ts replace the fetch(...) call inside attemptDelivery with a pinned node:https request. Import `request as httpsRequest` from node:https. Parse webhook.url, call resolveAndPinHost(parsed.hostname) to get the validated IP(s), then issue the POST via https.request with: host: parsed.hostname, port parsed.port||443, path parsed.pathname+parsed.search, method POST, the existing headers (Content-Type, X-Qivo-Event=delivery.event, X-Qivo-Timestamp, X-Qivo-Signature=computeSignature(secret, raw), User-Agent 'Qivo-Webhooks/1'), and a custom lookup(hostname, options, cb) that returns ONLY a pinned validated IP (cb(null, ip, family); when options.all is set, return the array form). Do NOT set rejectUnauthorized:false and do NOT override servername (defaults to hostname => TLS verified against the hostname). Apply a 10s timeout via req.setTimeout(WEBHOOK_TIMEOUT_MS, () => req.destroy(an AbortError-like error)). Write `raw` (JSON.stringify(delivery.payload)) as the body. In the response handler read only res.statusCode, then res.resume() (never parse the body). https.request does not follow redirects, so a 3xx is a non-2xx status (failure) — matching redirect:"manual". Preserve the exact status machine: ok on 2xx; lastError = `HTTP <status>` otherwise; 'timeout' on the timeout; 'blocked url' when WEBHOOK_URL_INVALID is thrown; 'network error: <msg>' otherwise. Wrap in a Promise so the existing async flow/await is preserved.

Extend apps/api/src/services/webhookDelivery.test.ts: keep all existing classifyAddress/isBlockedHostname cases; add selectPinnedAddresses tests (ok for all-public; ok:false when ANY address is private/loopback/link-local/metadata 169.254.169.254/IPv6-mapped-private; ok:false for empty list). Add an assertSafeWebhookUrl test that mocks node:dns/promises lookup (vi.mock) so a hostname resolving to a public IP is allowed and one resolving to a private IP is rejected with WEBHOOK_URL_INVALID. Do NOT hit the network.
acceptance_criteria: `cd apps/api && pnpm exec tsc --project tsconfig.json --noEmit` exits 0.

`cd apps/api && pnpm test` is green: public IP allowed; private/loopback/link-local/metadata/IPv6-mapped blocked; a hostname resolving to a private IP is rejected; selectPinnedAddresses selects only all-public lists and rejects when any is private.

attemptDelivery connects via a pinned validated public IP (custom lookup), TLS certificate verification remains enabled against the original hostname (rejectUnauthorized default true, servername defaults to hostname), redirects are still not followed, and the 10s timeout is preserved.
No new runtime dependency is added (undici is NOT introduced); https-only, hostname blocklist, and create-time validation all still hold; signing path and headers unchanged.
verification: cd apps/api ; pnpm exec tsc --project tsconfig.json --noEmit ; pnpm test
findings: Implemented in apps/api/src/services/webhookDelivery.ts. Added pure selectPinnedAddresses (ok:false on empty or any 'blocked' address via classifyAddress; else ok:true with all addresses) and async resolveAndPinHost (literal IP classified directly; else dns/promises lookup{all:true} -> selectPinnedAddresses; throws WEBHOOK_URL_INVALID on blocked/empty). assertSafeWebhookUrl now delegates its per-address loop to selectPinnedAddresses so create-time and send-time share one source of truth; its https-only check, isBlockedHostname check, and exact throw messages are unchanged. attemptDelivery's fetch() was replaced by node:https request via new sendPinnedRequest(): parses URL, re-checks https-only + isBlockedHostname, calls resolveAndPinHost, and issues POST with host=parsed.hostname, port=parsed.port||443, path=pathname+search, the unchanged signed headers (X-Qivo-Event/Timestamp/Signature + User-Agent 'Qivo-Webhooks/1'), and a custom lookup that returns ONLY the pinned IP(s) (single-cb and {all:true} array forms). rejectUnauthorized is left default (true) and servername is not overridden, so TLS verifies against the original hostname. https.request does not follow redirects, so a 3xx is a non-2xx failure (matches former redirect:'manual'). 10s timeout via req.setTimeout(WEBHOOK_TIMEOUT_MS) destroying the request with an AbortError-named error. Body (JSON.stringify(payload)) is written; response body is drained (res.resume()) and never parsed. Status machine preserved exactly: ok on 2xx; lastError 'HTTP <status>' on non-2xx; 'timeout' on timeout; 'blocked url' on WEBHOOK_URL_INVALID; 'network error: <msg>' otherwise. No new runtime dependency (undici not introduced). Tests extended with selectPinnedAddresses cases and a vi.mock('node:dns/promises') assertSafeWebhookUrl test (public allowed; private/mixed rejected) — no network. Verification: `pnpm exec tsc --project tsconfig.json --noEmit` exit 0; `pnpm test` green (184 passed, incl. 38 in webhookDelivery.test.ts). Residual risk: the lookup is cast to `never` to satisfy node:https LookupFunction typing under strict TS (runtime behaviour is correct for both callback forms). Pinning closes the validate-then-connect DNS-rebinding window for the hostname path; literal-IP targets are classified directly. TLS still trusts the system CA set; no additional certificate pinning beyond hostname verification.
